title: Fourier coefficient under coordinate extension
statement: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g$ be a real-valued function on the $k$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $T$ be a finite set of its coordinates. Extend $g$ to the $(k+1)$-dimensional cube by ignoring the last coordinate. The Fourier coefficient of this extension at the set $T$ embedded among the first $k$ coordinates equals the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a real-valued function on the $k$-dimensional Boolean cube
$T$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\\{0,\\ldots,k-1\\}$
